text.p: Former colonial power France appealed on Sunday for an immediate cease-fire in Cambodia and advised its nationals there to remain at home as fighting raged in the capital Phnom Penh for a second day.
"We advise prudence," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.

The ministry later said it had no information that any French nationals had been hurt in the fighting and could not immediately say how many French nationals there were in Cambodia, a French protectorate for 90 years until independence in 1953.

Cambodian King Sihanouk, in Beijing for medical treatment, issued an appeal for an immediate end to the fighting in Phnom Penh and urged the country's rival prime ministers to quickly visit him to iron out their differences.

Forces loyal to Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and his former battlefield enemy, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, began fighting in the capital on Saturday and Sihanouk said the situation was grave.
The two prime ministers head a fractured coalition government formed after a United Nations-run election in 1993.
